subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of these metals is the most reactive?
questions.explain: Potassium sits at the top of the reactivity series and is the most reactive of these metals.

questions.q: Which two non-metals are usually included in the reactivity series for comparison?
questions.explain: Carbon and hydrogen are placed in the series as reference points that determine extraction and acid-reaction behaviour.

questions.q: In the reactivity series, where is carbon placed relative to zinc and aluminium?
questions.explain: Carbon lies between aluminium and zinc, so it can reduce zinc and iron oxides but not aluminium oxide.

questions.q: Which metal is the least reactive of the following?
questions.explain: Gold is near the bottom of the reactivity series and is very unreactive.

questions.q: When a metal reacts with an acid, which products are formed?
questions.explain: Metal + acid produces a salt plus hydrogen gas.

questions.q: When a reactive metal such as sodium reacts with water, which products form?
questions.explain: Reactive metals react with water to form a metal hydroxide and hydrogen gas.

questions.q: Which test confirms that the gas produced when a metal reacts with acid is hydrogen?
options: It gives a squeaky pop with a lighted splint
questions.explain: Hydrogen produces a characteristic squeaky pop when a lighted splint is held to it.

questions.q: By which method is aluminium extracted from its ore?
questions.explain: Aluminium is more reactive than carbon, so it is extracted by electrolysis of molten aluminium oxide.

questions.q: Which metal is found in the Earth as the uncombined (native) element?
questions.explain: Gold is so unreactive that it is found native, uncombined with other elements.

questions.q: In the blast furnace, which substance reduces iron(III) oxide to iron?
questions.explain: Carbon monoxide reduces iron(III) oxide to iron in the blast furnace.

questions.q: Why are metals near the top of the reactivity series described as more reactive?
options: They lose their outer electrons more easily
questions.explain: More reactive metals lose their outer electrons more readily to form positive ions.

questions.q: What is observed when a small piece of sodium is added to water?
options: It sinks and dissolves slowly with no gas
It floats, moves about and fizzes as gas is given off
It burns with a bright white flame under the water
questions.explain: Sodium floats, moves around the surface and fizzes as hydrogen is released.

questions.q: In a displacement reaction, a more reactive metal will:
options: Take the place of a less reactive metal in its compound
Take the place of a more reactive metal in its compound
questions.explain: A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its compound.

questions.q: Which word equation correctly describes a displacement reaction?
options: Magnesium + copper sulfate → magnesium sulfate + copper
Copper + magnesium sulfate → copper sulfate + magnesium
Magnesium + copper sulfate → magnesium oxide + copper
Copper + magnesium sulfate → magnesium + copper oxide
questions.explain: Magnesium is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper from copper sulfate.

questions.q: Why can iron be extracted using carbon but aluminium cannot?
options: Iron is less reactive than carbon while aluminium is more reactive
Iron is more reactive than carbon while aluminium is less reactive
Iron ore is cheaper than aluminium ore
Aluminium has a lower melting point
questions.explain: Carbon can only reduce oxides of metals less reactive than itself, so iron works but aluminium does not.

questions.q: Why is the method used to extract a metal linked to its position in the reactivity series?
options: More reactive metals hold their compounds together more strongly and are harder to extract
Less reactive metals are always extracted by electrolysis
All metals can be extracted by heating alone
More reactive metals are cheaper to extract
questions.explain: The more reactive a metal, the more strongly it bonds in its compound, so a more powerful extraction method is needed.

questions.q: Magnesium reacts more vigorously with dilute acid than zinc. What does this tell us?
options: Magnesium is more reactive than zinc
Zinc is more reactive than magnesium
questions.explain: A more vigorous reaction with acid indicates the metal is higher in the reactivity series.

questions.q: Which metal, if placed in copper sulfate solution, would NOT produce a displacement reaction?
questions.explain: Silver is less reactive than copper, so it cannot displace copper from its solution.

questions.q: A newly discovered metal X is more reactive than carbon. Which extraction method should be used?
questions.explain: Metals more reactive than carbon must be extracted by electrolysis.

questions.q: Metal Y displaces copper from copper sulfate but cannot displace iron from iron sulfate. Where does Y sit in the reactivity series?
questions.explain: Y is more reactive than copper but less reactive than iron, so it lies between them.

specSource: CCEA GCSE Chemistry (2017) specification; Metals & Reactivity Series
